source.title: Beyond Language Modeling: An Exploration of Multimodal Pretraining
source.authors: Shengbang Tong; David Fan; John Nguyen; Ellis Brown; Gao-Yue Zhou; Shengyi Qian; Boyang Zheng; Théophane Vallaeys; Junlin Han; Rob Fergus; Naila Murray; Marjan Ghazvininejad; Mike Lewis; Nicolas Ballas; Amir Bar; Michael Rabbat; Jakob Verbeek; Luke S. record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses Chinchilla-style IsoFLOP sweeps, held-out validation losses, and fitted compute-optimal parameter/token trends, applying the same type of scaling measurement in unified multimodal models.
record.gate_note: Scaling results in Section 7 bear directly on loss scaling and compute-optimal allocation. Other reported comparisons of visual encoders, data mixtures, and downstream capabilities are not rows here unless they measure a claim version’s named scaling behavior. The paper does not report a test in which fits from small runs are used to predict much larger runs.
record.test_reason: The study runs Chinchilla-style IsoFLOP sweeps on held-out loss and fits compute-optimal Nopt∝C^a and Dopt∝C^b. It does this for language and vision in from-scratch unified multimodal models, both dense and MoE. The method matches the originals, but the setting (joint text+diffusion training, MoE with active-parameter counting) is new, so T3 fits better than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find that dense language scaling is near Chinchilla-balanced (a≈0.47) while vision is more data-hungry (b≈0.63). MoE narrows the parameter-exponent gap from 0.10 to 0.05 by making language more data-hungry (b 0.53→0.59). Unified models match unimodal baselines at equal compute.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Chinchilla-style IsoFLOP sweeps and held-out validation losses, but applies them to from-scratch unified language–vision models, including MoE, rather than language-only models.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted compute-optimal exponents differ between language and vision and between dense and MoE architectures. The analysis uses held-out DCLM for language and CC12M for vision; the MoE results use a sparsity ratio of 16.

fits_no_version.finding: Unified multimodal models match unimodal baselines in language perplexity at equal compute. Dense: Notes 23.7 vs 23.8, DCLM 13.3 vs 13.6. MoE: DCLM 12.3 vs 12.0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Joint vision-language pretraining costs little language loss at fixed compute.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed active compute, increasing total experts from 32 to 1008 steadily lowers text loss and diffusion loss for RAE; VAE diffusion loss saturates (Figs. 16–17).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss improves with total (inactive) parameter count in MoE at fixed active compute.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates for the fitted exponents are reported. The loss-versus-compute curves are shown in figures without extractable numeric values or a text description of their shape. Scaling results cover the study’s tested data, models, and architectures only.
record.rows_left_out: No other directly relevant Section 7 results were omitted. Downstream-task, generation-score, and FID comparisons were not extracted because they do not measure the loss or allocation behavior named in the tested versions.

untested.parts: The paper fits L(C)=A·C^-α+E per model class (Figs. 24, 26), but reports no α, E or fit quality. No separate N or D loss exponents are reported.
No small-to-large prediction is checked. The 14×/51× data-ratio projections to 100B/1T parameters are untested extrapolations.
Stability of the exponent is not checked: a power law is assumed and a+b=1 is imposed. The compute range is about 6e18–1e21 FLOPs, and no uncertainty is given.
No depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count.
Video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer scaling are not tested. The vision loss-vs-compute power-law fit is figure-only.
Downstream metrics (DPG, FID) are plotted against compute, but their predictability is not analysed.
No alternative fitting methods, parameter-counting conventions or schedules are compared, and no curvature analysis is done.

missing.what: Power-law-plus-constant fit L(C)=A·C^-α+E to loss vs compute for each model class (Text-Only, T2I-Only, Dense/MoE Multimodal); α and E are not stated in text.
missing.locator: Section 7, Compute efficiency for dense models; Figs. 24, 26

missing.what: Projection that the vision/language optimal data ratio grows as N^0.57 (14× at 100B, 51× at 1T parameters), derived from the fitted exponents.

record.verdict_notes: Several features of the fits weaken them as tests: a+b=1 is imposed, a power law is assumed rather than tested, no confidence intervals are given, and compute spans only about 2.2 orders of magnitude. MoE uses active-parameter counting. Rows R5–R10 are single-point model comparisons, not scaling measures, so they are delinked. The record's V1 support label is dropped because no numeric loss power-law result is given in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The study fits loss against compute for dense models and reports IsoFLOP loss surfaces, but does not report separate fixed-other-factor loss exponents for parameters and tokens.
No explicit small-run fit is evaluated as a prediction of the loss of much larger runs.
The study reports fitted parameter and token exponents for dense and MoE language and vision models, but does not establish that the trends hold across other model families or setups.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count to measure their effect on loss.
Scaling is tested for vision in unified models, but not for standalone image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, or other modalities.
The study reports downstream evaluations elsewhere, but does not test whether downstream performance scales predictably with pretraining loss or scale.

Results show differences by modality and dense versus MoE architecture. The study does not compare alternative fitting methods or parameter-counting conventions, nor report systematic curve bending away from power laws.
